subject: Resulting DSM fit is very wrong despite significance in summary outputs

messages.author: cfb364282622bc71
messages.subject: Resulting DSM fit is very wrong despite significance in summary outputs
parts:
Dear Distance Samplers,

I am fitting a DSM on whale sightings. I have first included all variables and removed those that were not significant to a p<0.05 level for both NB and TW. (following the style of the vignette which are amazing!!) I am left with spatial and SST (although SST could be added as a linear term due to the edf being close to 1 am i correct?). I have analysed both through till the end, but for sake of simplicity I will talk about the model: s(x,y) + s(SST). I have attached the summary output for this model.

When I go to produce the DSM predictions dsm.xy.pred_A2_ST_nb <- predict(A2_3_ST_nb, preddataA2, preddataA2$area) I get the following spatial map (attached).

I have been having trouble understanding why the DSM I am producing in R looks very wrong compared to the sightings distribution. I have been searching the comments for a few days now and have tried a few bits of code to see whether there are any problems with the model fit (e.g. I thought perhaps the model was not an ovedispersion of zeros so have tried model$data$count as well as fitting a gam ~poisson...which did not look right either for model outputs like q-q plots. Below is the model$count output:

> A2_3_ST_nb$data$count

 [1]  0  3  5  0  0  0  2  4  5  0  2  2  4  2  0  0  0  0  0  3  0  0  4  0  5  0  2 10  2  0  0  0  4  0  7  0  0  0  0  0  0  4  2  1  0  0  0  2  0  1  0  0  0  0  2  0  0  0  0  0  1  1  1  0

[65]  4  0  3  1  0  0) 

I have also tried plotting the model with spatial smooth as this was also significant on it's own, and the resulting output again doesn't seem right. It looks like my bottom left (where there are no sightings) is having a lot of the power. As a result the abundance estimates also seem very wrong.

Perhaps my prediction grid is wrong, but this has not caused me problems for other DSM models.


If something screams out as wrong in the summary output or if there are ways to avoid edge effects I would appreciate the feedback.

Thank you so much for your time,

Raphael

I'm afraid I don't have any clear answers for you, but I share your concern about the disconnect between your sightings and the predicted surface.  I realise you models of interest do not contain depth, but I note in passing from your tabular prediction grid that all but one of your first 20 rows have depth of 0, but have SST values and consequently predicted whale abundances.

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Resulting DSM fit is very wrong despite significance in summary outputs
parts:
Hi Raphael, hi listfolk,

Following-on from Eric's point (which is certainly worth investigation),
it's worth plotting the SST surface and seeing if there may be problems
there (in how it was processed) that may give these strange answers (SST
data might be fine for the model data but not for the prediction grid.
Checking the range of the SST in the model vs prediction grid may be
useful here too (extrapolating outside of the data is a good way to get
weird answers).

If the EDF of the SST term is ~1, as you say you have something close to
a linear effect. That could be causing issues. A different approach here
might be to include your covariates using the bs="ts" option, which can
"remove" the covariate (estimate an effect size of 0) if it's not a good
predictor (whereas normally we can only take the EDF to 1). Trying
s(SST, bs="ts") might show that SST is not to useful (though to be fully
coherent here you'd really need to go back and use this for all your
model selection, see e.g.
http://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-dsm-2020/practicals/03-multiple-smooths_solution.html).

Hope this helps,
--dave

Hi All,

Thanks for all your contributions and suggestions and as a result I think I may have figured out what the problem could be - correct me if I am wrong/going down a wrong tangent.

Firstly to answer Robs question. If I am right in what you are saying, I have already checked my x and y limits of my prediction grid and they are larger than my largest and smallest x and y sightings. Actually I think this is where this prediction is going wrong like it was brought up by Stephen. The prediction grid is a larger rectangular grid that encompasses my study area. The bottom left corner is an island which was obviously not surveyed (please find attached: survey area example with prediction grid example). What I was hoping to achieve was to intersect the survey area over the larger prediction grid at a later stage if that makes sense. This is because I have had trouble with making my prediction grid (although I have followed http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/mexico-analysis.html, which has been very useful), I can't seem to export my resulting "study-area shaped" DSM into a shapefile for GIS use later. (please note this larger grid is only done for the prediction stage).



This must be why I am getting a higher density in the bottom left, as sightings in the bottom left of the survey area are being extrapolated to the non surveyed area of the prediction grid (?) like mentioned by Stephen. I think I should therefore try again with coding my survey area as a prediction grid itself and this may sort the issue out.

To answer Eric's and David's message about SST: Where the depth is zero is where the land is. I have done it so that I also made SST = 0 whenever depth was zero to mirror land data, but I don't think that made much of a difference. I will have a go at checking my SST range however, as this is good practice and I should incorporate this check nevertheless. In terms of the bs="ts", I have found that they do make some of my variables significant, but then the resulting visgam for these models always seem to concentrate densities within a small corner. Without "ts" this does not happen and the resulting visgams seem more "normal". However, some "ts" models seem good, so perhaps this comes back to my prediction grid?\

Thanks again for your quick replied and good suggestions,

Raph
